clue.text: In great trepidation, chose to include article

indicators.note: the word for chose takes the article inside it, so it holds the other piece

parts.note: to choose is to pick, so chose means picked
an is the indefinite article in grammar

explanation.surface: Someone nervously chooses to put an article into a piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' tempts a solver to think of a newspaper piece, but it is the grammatical article, and 'to include' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in great trepidation is gripped by sudden fear, the state of having lost their head.

clue.text: Springbok's ready to dive in a wee bit haphazardly

indicators.note: the South African money plunges into the tiny particle, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an atom is a very small bit of anything
ready is slang for cash, and the Springbok stands for South Africa, whose currency is the rand

explanation.surface: A South African rugby player is poised to plunge in, a little chaotically.
explanation.walkthrough: Springboks is the name of South Africa's rugby team, so 'Springbok's' means South African; 'ready' (as in 'the readies') is cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without plan or pattern is doing it haphazardly, by chance.

clue.text: Children's edition

explanation.surface: A note about a children's version of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are one's issue in legal language, and a magazine's edition is an issue of it.

clue.text: Refuse to be upset, and don't accept wigging?

explanation.surface: Someone stays calm and declines to wear a wig.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the idiom for staying calm; the second reads it literally, keeping your own locks rather than taking a wig.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means stay calm, and literally refusing a wig means keeping your natural locks in place.

clue.text: Fed up with performance — nothing working effectively?

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word Fed is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written before being turned round
an act is a performance on stage
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone tired of a show finds nothing in it working properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' looks like boredom, but 'up' turns FED into DEF in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'in fact': a de facto ruler is one in actual control, operating in practice whatever the law says.

clue.text: Material was touching

explanation.surface: A note that a piece of fabric was making contact.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressed wool fabric bears this name, and it is also the past tense of the verb meaning to touch or sense.

clue.text: Is shooting expedition a projected item?

parts.note: to shoot a movie is to film it, so 'is shooting' gives the verb form films
a trip is a journey or expedition

explanation.surface: A question whether a hunting expedition is a planned event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shooting' suggests guns, but here it means filming with a camera.
explanation.definitionFit: A length of photographic stills shown on a screen by a projector is a projected item.

clue.text: A case of peas with fish served up — get stuck in

indicators.note: the word for getting stuck goes inside the reversed fish
in a down clue served up means the fish is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an eel is a long snake-like fish
to gum is to stick things together, so things gummed get stuck

explanation.surface: A tin of peas served with fish, and diners told to tuck in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' is a reversal only because this is a down clue; 'get stuck in' looks like an invitation to eat, but 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pod is the botanical case enclosing peas or beans, and the pod is the source of this word.

clue.text: Create extra strain, sort life crises can produce

indicators.note: the jumbled phrase is able to yield a new arrangement of its letters

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Tackling your midlife problems might cause more stress than it cures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' looks like stress, but it is a plant or animal variety: mixing two varieties produces a new one.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollinating one plant from another variety breeds a hybrid, a new strain.

clue.text: Swears blind it's a fish

indicators.note: swearing blind is cursing wildly, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone insists that something is a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swears blind' reads as insisting, but 'blind' signals rearranging SWEARS.
explanation.definitionFit: A brightly coloured sea fish of rocky coasts goes by this name.

clue.text: Supporter of stag, for example, but not hind

definitions.text: Supporter of stag, for example, but not hind

parts.words: Supporter of stag, for example, but not hind
parts.note: a stag stands on limbs; the one meant is at the front, not the back

explanation.surface: Something that supports male deer, but not females.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hind' seems to be the female deer beside 'stag', but it means rear: the limb is the front one, not the back one.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's front limb is one that props it up, at the front rather than the rear.

clue.text: Nice hour's play — not over-adventurous

indicators.note: the letters are allowed to play freely and settle in a new order

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter; the word is hour

explanation.surface: An hour spent on the French Riviera at Nice is not very daring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like an adjective, but its letters, with HOUR, are the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking courage or daring is the opposite of brave, so not over-adventurous.

clue.text: Mostly plant identical type of seeds

indicators.note: most of the word for plant, losing its last letter

parts.note: to set seedlings is to plant them
identical means the same

explanation.surface: Nearly all the plants are identical seed varieties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' cuts SET to SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Small oily seeds from an Asian plant, scattered on bread rolls, bear this name.

clue.text: Alternative suggestion from bartender?

parts.note: a revised bid in negotiation, read as what a barman proposes across his bar

explanation.surface: A barman proposes a different idea.
explanation.walkthrough: A bartender serves across the bar top, so what they offer comes over the counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply bid made in place of the first proposal is an alternative suggestion in negotiation.

clue.text: Weed out such signs in public places?

definitions.text: Weed out such signs in public places?

parts.words: Weed out such signs in public places?
parts.note: weed is slang for tobacco, and these notices put it out in public places

explanation.surface: Gardening notices urging people to clear weeds in public parks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weed out' reads as gardening, but 'weed' is tobacco: the signs ban lighting up.
explanation.definitionFit: Notices banning cigarettes appear in public places, telling people tobacco is out.

clue.text: Cost of great PC I fancy

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, telling us to rework the letters

explanation.surface: How much does a great computer I'd like cost?
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like 'want', but it signals rearranging GREATPCI.
explanation.definitionFit: The label on goods shows what they sell for, their cost.

clue.text: Form to be filled in, assessing each of its members?

definitions.text: Form to be filled in, assessing each of its members?

parts.words: Form to be filled in, assessing each of its members?
parts.note: a form is a school class, and teachers write a document assessing every pupil in it

explanation.surface: A paperwork form to complete, rating everyone in an organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' looks like paperwork, but in British schools a form is a class of pupils; each pupil gets a written assessment at term's end.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher's written account of a pupil's progress is filled in for each member of a class.

clue.text: Grabbing iron, drove wildly, getting a stuffing?

indicators.note: the jumbled word takes hold of the iron symbol, putting it inside
driving wildly means the letters of drove are thrown about

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A reckless driver seizing a golf iron gets a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges the driver's word to OVERD before 'Grabbing' takes in the iron symbol; the question mark flags that being overfed is likened to a stuffed bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone given far too much to eat is stuffed, like a turkey getting its stuffing.

clue.text: Born with talent, leading to Hound Dog …

parts.note: b is the abbreviation for born, as in family trees
a talent is an asset

explanation.surface: Someone born gifted goes on to make the song Hound Dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the next clue: 'Hound Dog' is also the song in 21 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-legged, long-eared breed of hound is a kind of dog.

clue.text: In a political section seen to be dying?

indicators.note: a section is a part cut from the run of words, so the answer lies inside them

explanation.surface: A question about someone in a political group who appears to be fading.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the saying 'See Naples and die', so the Italian name for Naples is the place seen before dying.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'See Naples and die' means a visit to the Italian city is the last sight worth having.

clue.text: I've rejected stupid-sounding clues, perhaps

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken without its apostrophe

indicators.note: the word for stupid is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: dense means stupid

explanation.surface: Someone turns down clues that seem foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns IVE into EVI; 'sounding' signals DENSE heard as DENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Clues are an example of what a detective gathers as proof.

clue.text: … which I sang live, rocking with a bit of style

indicators.note: rocking means shaking, so the letters of live are moved about
only the first letter of style is taken

explanation.surface: Continuing from Hound Dog: a song I performed on stage, rocking stylishly.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues from 18 down: the singer of Hound Dog is speaking as 'I'.
explanation.definitionFit: The King of rock and roll recorded the hit Hound Dog, so the song is one he sang.

clue.text: By-product of politician's ploy not acceptable

parts.note: spin is a politician's presentation of facts in a favourable light
off means not acceptable, as in 'that's a bit off'

explanation.surface: A side effect of a politician's trick turns out to be unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' in British speech means unacceptable or out of order.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary product or show derived from an original is a by-product of it.

clue.text: Request one number quickly

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
vite is French and musical for quickly

explanation.surface: Asking for one musical number to be played fast.
explanation.walkthrough: VITE is French for quickly, also used as a musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask someone to come along is to request their presence.

clue.text: Like a party before the match? Time to drop round

definitions.text: Like a party before the match?

indicators.note: the word for drop goes round the time letter

parts.note: to sag is to droop or drop

explanation.surface: A pre-match party where it's time to drop by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' means a marriage: the party is the groom's night out before the wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A party held for the groom before his wedding is named after the male deer.

clue.text: Display by disciplined performer mounted in period costume? Just the opposite

indicators.note: the pieces appear in reverse order, so costume comes first, then period

parts.note: dress means costume
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A show by a horse-riding performer in historical costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'period costume' would give the period first; 'Just the opposite' puts the costume first. The 'performer mounted' is a horse and rider.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse and rider performing precise trained movements put on a display of equestrian discipline.
